record.context_brief: Fast mixing up to beta*=1 in SK model
record.original_question: Consider the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with interaction matrix J = beta W where W ~ GOE(n), with an arbitrary external field, and Glauber dynamics for sampling from the Gibbs measure on {+1,-1}^n. Does Glauber dynamics mix in polynomial time for all beta up to the replica-symmetry-breaking threshold beta* = 1?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15. Consider the SK-model with an arbitrary external field. Does Glauber Dynamics fast mix (meaning in polynomial time) up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold β∗ = 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $W$ be an $n \times n$ matrix drawn from the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (i.e., $W$ is symmetric with $W_{ii} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,2/n)$ and $W_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1/n)$ for $i < j$, all independent). Fix $\beta > 0$ and an external field vector $h \in \mathbb{R}^n$, and define the Gibbs measure on the hypercube $\{-1,+1\}^n$ by
$$\mu(\sigma) \;=\; \frac{1}{Z}\exp\!\Big(\tfrac{\beta}{2}\,\langle \sigma, W\sigma\rangle + \langle h,\sigma\rangle\Big),$$
where $Z$ is the normalizing partition function. The (single-site) Glauber dynamics is the discrete-time Markov chain on $\{-1,+1\}^n$ that at each step selects a coordinate $i \in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ uniformly at random and resamples $\sigma_i$ from its conditional law under $\mu$ given the remaining coordinates; this chain is reversible with respect to $\mu$.

The replica-symmetry-breaking threshold of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model is $\beta^* = 1$.

Question: Is it true that for every $\beta < 1$ and for every external field $h \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for $\mu$ is bounded by a polynomial in $n$ (with high probability over $W$ as $n \to \infty$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is open. The best known polynomial mixing-time bound for Glauber dynamics on the SK model holds only up to $\beta < 0.295$ (Anari–Koehler–Vuong, 2024). Alternative samplers based on stochastic localization and Approximate Message Passing achieve sampling (in Wasserstein distance) up to $\beta < 1/2$ (El Alaoui–Montanari–Sellke) and were recently extended by Celentano to all $\beta < 1$, but these are not Glauber dynamics. Whether Glauber dynamics itself mixes in polynomial time up to $\beta^*=1$ remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Sampling from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model (problem 15) | Randomstrasse 101
status_evidence.snippet: Glauber dynamics alone has only reached β < 0.295 in total variation distance ... fundamental question of whether Glauber dynamics specifically can achieve fast mixing up to β = 1 ... remains unsolved.
status_evidence.claim: The problem remains open; best Glauber bound is β<0.295.

status_evidence.title: Exponentially slow mixing of the low temperature SK model
status_evidence.snippet: Sellke shows exponentially slow mixing of Glauber dynamics for the SK model at low temperature.
status_evidence.claim: Low-temperature (β large) Glauber dynamics is exponentially slow, consistent with the threshold being at most β*=1.
